record.title: Entry record
record.description: One file per term, named for the term's slug. Every audience reads this file: the README, the site, and the issue form a contributor fills in.

issue.name: New entry
issue.description: Propose a term for the Civic Bestiary
issue.intro: Thanks for proposing a term. Pick the kind of thing you are naming first - a species is an actor you can point at, a move is an action you can watch, an ability is a capability an institution wields, a format is a medium that stages the others, and a buff is a temporary condition. Then fill in what you can; the maintainers handle placement, cross-references, and the final edit.
issue.identification_hint: Describe it the way its kind is described. Species: range, call, field marks. Move: trigger, tell, counter. Ability: effect, available to, counter. Format: carriers, economics, signature. Buff: effect, tell, expires.
issue.outro: A proposal lands as a record under `data/entries/` once the writing holds up. The bar is not novelty, it is use: the term should name something a reader recognises and has no word for yet.

species.label: Species
species.blurb: An actor you can point at: the person running the bit.

identification.label: Range
identification.hint: Where you meet it. Concrete places, not abstractions - truck beds, county fairs, a specific comment section.
identification.example: Truck beds, county fairs, and the comment section under any local news post.

identification.label: Call
identification.hint: The thing it says. A short quotation, ideally something you have actually heard.

identification.label: Field marks
identification.hint: How you recognise it at a distance. Three is the house number.
identification.example: Flag decal on a leased vehicle

move.label: Move
move.blurb: An action performed in the open, in front of witnesses.

identification.label: Trigger
identification.hint: The moment it gets played - what has just happened that makes this the move to make.
identification.example: A question it cannot answer is on the floor.

identification.label: Tell
identification.hint: What the move looks like from the gallery. The visible behaviour, not the motive.
identification.example: A request for definitions, repeated until the clock runs out.

identification.label: Counter
identification.hint: The thing that ends it, or makes it cost more than it returns.
identification.example: Answer the question once, in writing, and move to close.

ability.label: Ability
ability.blurb: A capability an office, body, or machine can wield - no single person owns it.

identification.label: Effect
identification.hint: What it does to the board, in one sentence.
identification.example: Converts a map into a majority before a single vote is cast.

identification.label: Available to
identification.hint: Who can play it: an office, a chamber, a platform, a committee.
identification.example: State legislatures, once a decade, in a room with no cameras.

identification.label: Counter
identification.hint: The rule, court, or practice that blunts it.
identification.example: An independent commission with a map-drawing mandate.

format.label: Format
format.blurb: A medium that stages the others - the show, not the performer.

identification.label: Carriers
identification.hint: Where the format lives: which channels, slots, or platforms.
identification.example: Cable primetime, streaming specials, and the merch drop that follows.

identification.label: Economics
identification.example: Ad rates keyed to outrage, plus a subscription tier for the uncut version.

identification.label: Signature
identification.hint: The unmistakable formal tic - what makes it recognisably this format and not the news.
identification.example: A countdown clock over a battlefield.

buff.label: Buff
buff.blurb: A temporary condition that changes what a creature can get away with.

identification.label: Effect
identification.hint: What it changes about the bearer's behaviour or standing.
identification.example: Excuses any contradiction for the length of the news cycle.

identification.label: Tell
identification.hint: How you spot someone carrying it.
identification.example: Confident mispronunciation of a thing they claim to have served in.

identification.label: Expires
identification.hint: What ends it, and roughly when.
identification.example: The first primary debate, or the first subpoena - whichever lands first.

uses.label: Uses
uses.hint: The creature or format wields this capability.

stages.label: Stages
stages.hint: The format is the place this happens; the creature or move is what fills it.

counters.label: Counters
counters.hint: The play that ends it. Author one direction only - the inverse page renders the other.

fields.label: Term
fields.hint: The coinage, spelled the way it should be listed. Title case, no quotes.

fields.label: Kind
fields.hint: What sort of thing this is. A species is a person-shaped pattern, a move is an action, an ability belongs to an office, a format is a show, and a buff is a condition.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.hint: Which chapter the entry belongs to. The maintainers will move it if it belongs elsewhere.

fields.label: Position in chapter
fields.hint: Where the entry sits inside its chapter. Appending means one past the current highest.

fields.label: Part of speech
fields.hint: What the term is grammatically. Most species are nouns; moves are usually gerunds.

fields.label: Pronunciation
fields.hint: IPA between slashes. Approximate is fine.

fields.label: Etymology
fields.hint: Where the word came from, in one line. Name both parents if it is a blend.

fields.label: Senses
fields.hint: Two definitions: the thing itself, then the pattern it runs. Full sentences, one per line. The first sense becomes the page description, so make it stand alone.
fields.example: A citizen who performs patriotism as a shield while undermining the civic obligations it claims to honour.

fields.label: Example
fields.hint: One sentence in the wild, with the term in bold. Wrap the quotation in *asterisks*; the README renders it as an aside.
fields.example: *"He wrapped himself in the flag at every rally, yet his refusal to respect basic civic responsibilities showed he was more of a **playtriot** than a true patriot."*

fields.label: Easily confused with
fields.hint: Existing terms it could be mistaken for, and the one thing that tells them apart. Optional at proposal time - the maintainers add twins when the confusion is real.
fields.example: LARPtarian - both dress the part; the playtriot buys the flag, the LARPtarian buys the surplus rifle.

fields.label: Cross-references
fields.hint: Two or three existing terms this one belongs beside. The graph must stay connected, so every term needs at least one inbound reference.

fields.label: Typed links
fields.hint: Relationship edges to other entries, each with a relation from the schema's vocabulary. Author one direction; the other page shows the inverse automatically.
